observations_ko.deficiency_ko: 귀사는 수산화알루미늄 보조제 제조에 사용되는 전용 장비의 세척 절차에 대해 오염 또는 이월(carry-over)을 방지하도록 밸리데이션하지 않았다.
observations_ko.detail_ko: 이 보조제는 Infanrix, Boostrix, Kinrix, Pediarix를 포함한 귀사의 미국 허가 제품의 구성 성분이다. 구체적으로, 수산화알루미늄 보조제 생산 구역 ((비공개) 및 (비공개))에 대한 귀사의 세척 밸리데이션 및 모니터링 프로그램이 부적절하다. 귀사는 밸리데이션되지 않은 (비공개) 세척 단계를 일상 생산에 도입했고, 밸리데이션된 (비공개) 세척 공정의 관리 상태를 유지하지 못했으며, 반복되는 세척 실패를 적절히 조사하지 못했다. a) 귀사는 밸리데이션되지 않은 (비공개) 임시방편(workaround)을 일상적인 세척 및 제조 공정에 도입했다. 2023년 5월 이후 귀사는 수산화알루미늄 보조제의 모든 배치에 대해 (비공개)을(를) 사용하는 밸리데이션되지 않은 (비공개) 세척 절차를 사용해 왔다. 이 절차는 수산화알루미늄 (비공개)의 알려진 설계 결함을 완화하기 위해 도입되었으며, (2026년 1월 도입된) (비공개) 및 (2023년 5월 도입된) (비공개)이(가) 있고 (비공개)이다. 이 (비공개) 세척 단계는 그 효과를 입증하도록 밸리데이션되지 않았다. 더욱이 귀사의 세척 공정에 대한 이 변경은 귀사의 변경관리 시스템을 통해 관리되지 않았다.

observations_ko.deficiency_ko: 배치가 이미 유통되었는지 여부와 관계없이 설명되지 않는 불일치를 철저히 검토하지 못했다.
observations_ko.detail_ko: 구체적으로, 귀사는 수산화알루미늄 보조제 충전 장비와 관련된 (비공개) 시험 결과 부적합에 대해 SOP-082366 「일탈 처리」에 따른 공식 조사를 수행하지 못했다. SOP 9000087625 「(비공개)에 대한 요구사항」 (원문 여기서 끊김)

observations_ko.deficiency_ko: 문서화된 시료채취 계획, 시험 절차 및 실험실 메커니즘으로부터의 일탈이 정당화되지 않는다.
observations_ko.detail_ko: 구체적으로, ERVEBO 완제의약품 백신 및 관련 물질의 안정성 시험에 사용되는 귀사의 위탁 시험 실험실에서 발생한 설명되지 않은 불일치를 철저히 검토하지 못했다. 예를 들어, (비공개)의 위탁 시험 실험실은 ERVEBO 백신(재조합 수포성 구내염 바이러스-자이르 에볼라 생약독화 바이러스)의 안정성 시험을 수행하는 데 사용된다. 2019년부터 2023년까지 이 위탁 시험 실험실에서 발생한 18건의 안정성 일탈 중 7건이 누락된 안정성 시점, 세포 역가 시험에 만료된 배지 사용, 시료 관리 오류, 시험 중 잘못된 온도의 시료 보관 및 기타 사유를 포함한 다양한 이유로 발생했다. 귀사는 위탁 시험 실험실이 안정성 시료를 관리하고 안정성 시험을 올바르게 수행하고 있음을 보증하기 위해 이러한 일탈을 충분히 조사하지 않았다.

key_violations.original: Your firm failed to have, for each batch of drug product, appropriate laboratory determination of satisfactory conformance to final specifications for the drug product, including the identity and strength of each active ingredient, prior to release; and, your firm failed to conduct appropriate laboratory testing, as necessary, for each batch of drug product required to be free of objectionable microorganisms (21 CFR 211.165(a) and 211.165(b)). Your firm manufactures sunscreen drug products. Based on the records and information you provided, you did not demonstrate that you conduct adequate finished drug product testing on your drug products. Specifically, neither the certificate of analysis (COA) reports nor the batch records that you provided include an appropriate assay test for active ingredient content or impurity testing. In addition, your records do not include appropriate microbiological testing. Full release testing, including strength and identity testing of the active ingredient, as well as appropriate microbiological testing, must be performed before drug product release and distribution. Without adequate testing, you do not have adequate scientific evidence to ensure that your drug products conform to appropriate specifications before release.
key_violations.description: 귀사는 각 의약품 배치에 대해 출하 전에 각 유효성분의 확인(identity) 및 함량(strength)을 포함하여 완제품 최종 규격에 대한 적합성을 적절한 시험실 시험으로 판정하지 않았으며, 또한 불쾌미생물(objectionable microorganisms)이 없어야 하는 각 의약품 배치에 대해 필요한 적절한 시험실 시험을 실시하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.165(a) 및 211.165(b)). 귀사는 자외선차단제(선스크린) 의약품을 제조한다. 귀사가 제출한 기록과 정보에 근거할 때, 귀사는 자사 의약품에 대해 적절한 완제품 시험을 실시하고 있음을 입증하지 못했다. 구체적으로, 귀사가 제출한 시험성적서(COA)와 배치 기록 어디에도 유효성분 함량에 대한 적절한 정량(assay) 시험이나 불순물 시험이 포함되어 있지 않았다. 또한 귀사의 기록에는 적절한 미생물 시험도 포함되어 있지 않다. 유효성분의 함량 및 확인 시험과 적절한 미생물 시험을 포함한 전항목 출하 시험은 의약품의 출하 및 유통 전에 반드시 수행되어야 한다. 적절한 시험 없이는 출하 전에 의약품이 적절한 규격에 적합함을 보증할 충분한 과학적 근거를 갖출 수 없다.
key_violations.risk: 정량·불순물·미생물 시험 없이 선스크린 제품이 출하되어, 함량 미달·불순물 초과·미생물 오염 제품이 미국 시장에 유통되었을 가능성을 배제할 수 없다.

key_violations.original: Your firm failed to conduct at least one test to verify the identity of each component of a drug product. Your firm also failed to validate and establish the reliability of your component supplier’s test analyses at appropriate intervals (21 CFR 211.84(d)(1) and 211.84(d)(2)). Based on the records and information you provided, you did not demonstrate that you are adequately testing the identity of incoming components used in the manufacture of your drug products. Your response also indicated that you accept your supplier’s COA without verifying the test results at appropriate intervals. Verification of component quality is performed only by reviewing the COAs and material safety data sheets provided by the suppliers. Without adequate testing and without establishing the reliability of your component suppliers’ test analyses at appropriate intervals, you do not have scientific evidence that your raw materials conform to appropriate specifications before you use them in the manufacture of your drug products. As a manufacturer, you have a responsibility to sample, test, and examine drug components before you use them in production to ensure adequate quality.
key_violations.description: 귀사는 의약품의 각 원료(component)에 대해 확인(identity)을 검증하는 시험을 최소 1개 이상 실시하지 않았다. 또한 귀사는 원료 공급업체 시험 분석의 신뢰성을 적절한 주기로 밸리데이션하고 확립하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.84(d)(1) 및 211.84(d)(2)). 귀사가 제출한 기록과 정보에 근거할 때, 귀사는 의약품 제조에 사용되는 입고 원료의 확인 시험을 적절히 수행하고 있음을 입증하지 못했다. 귀사의 회신은 또한 귀사가 공급업체의 COA를 적절한 주기로 그 시험 결과를 검증하지 않은 채 그대로 수용하고 있음을 보여주었다. 원료 품질의 검증은 공급업체가 제공한 COA와 물질안전보건자료를 검토하는 방식으로만 이루어지고 있다. 적절한 시험 없이, 그리고 원료 공급업체 시험 분석의 신뢰성을 적절한 주기로 확립하지 않고서는, 원료가 의약품 제조에 사용되기 전에 적절한 규격에 적합하다는 과학적 근거를 갖출 수 없다. 제조업자로서 귀사는 적절한 품질을 보증하기 위해 생산에 사용하기 전에 의약품 원료를 검체 채취·시험·검사할 책임이 있다.
key_violations.risk: 공급업체 COA에만 의존해 확인 시험 없이 원료를 투입하므로, 잘못된 원료나 오염·부적합 원료가 그대로 제품에 혼입될 위험이 있다.

key_violations.original: Your firm’s quality unit failed to exercise its responsibility to ensure drug products manufactured are in compliance with CGMP and meet established specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.22). Based on the records and information you provided, your firm failed to establish an adequate quality unit (QU) with the responsibilities and authority to oversee the manufacturing of drug products. For example, your QU failed to ensure: Adequate procedures ensuring appropriate production and process controls for drug product manufacturing and qualification of equipment used to manufacture drug products (21 CFR 211.100(a)). Adequate laboratory control procedures to ensure drug products conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.160(b)). The establishment of an adequate, ongoing stability program (21 CFR 211.166(a)). Your firm’s quality systems are inadequate.
key_violations.description: 귀사의 품질부서는 제조된 의약품이 CGMP를 준수하고 확인(identity)·함량(strength)·품질(quality)·순도(purity)에 대해 설정된 규격을 충족하도록 보증할 책임을 이행하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.22). 귀사가 제출한 기록과 정보에 근거할 때, 귀사는 의약품 제조를 감독할 책임과 권한을 갖춘 적절한 품질부서(QU)를 확립하지 않았다. 예를 들어, 귀사의 QU는 다음 사항을 보증하지 못했다. 의약품 제조를 위한 적절한 생산 및 공정 관리와 의약품 제조에 사용되는 설비의 적격성평가를 보장하는 적절한 절차(21 CFR 211.100(a)). 의약품이 확인·함량·품질·순도에 관한 적절한 기준에 적합하도록 보장하는 적절한 시험실 관리 절차(21 CFR 211.160(b)). 적절하고 지속적인 안정성 시험 프로그램의 수립(21 CFR 211.166(a)). 귀사의 품질 시스템은 부적절하다.
key_violations.risk: 품질부서가 공정·설비·시험실·안정성 관리를 감독하지 못해 개별 위반이 아닌 품질 시스템 전반의 결함으로 판단되며, 출하 판정의 신뢰성 자체가 무너진다.

deep_analysis.fda_evaluation: FDA는 2025년 9월 9일자 704(a)(4) 기록 요청과 후속 서신에 따라 귀사가 제출한 기록·정보를 검토한 결과, 귀사의 방법·시설·관리가 CGMP에 부합하지 않아 의약품이 불량(adulterated)에 해당한다고 판단했다. 귀사는 완제품 출하 시험(유효성분 정량·불순물·미생물 시험)과 입고 원료 확인 시험을 적절히 수행하고 있음을 입증하지 못했으며, 귀사의 회신 자체가 공급업체 COA를 주기적 검증 없이 수용하고 COA와 물질안전보건자료 검토만으로 원료 품질을 확인하고 있음을 드러냈다고 지적했다. 또한 품질부서가 생산·공정 관리, 시험실 관리, 안정성 프로그램을 보증하지 못해 품질 시스템 전체가 부적절하다고 평가했다. 위반의 성격상 21 CFR 211.34에 따른 자격 있는 컨설턴트를 고용해 운영 전반에 대한 6개 시스템 감사와 CAPA 완료·효과성 평가를 받을 것을 권고했으며, 컨설턴트 고용이 경영진의 CGMP 준수 책임을 면제하지 않는다고 명시했다.

required_remediation.deadline: 서한 수령 후 15영업일 이내 CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov 로 서면 회신(이메일 제목에 FEI 3023093622 및 ATTN: Bryce Hammer 기재).
items: 각 배치의 출하 판정 전에 사용하는 화학·미생물 규격 및 시험방법 목록을 제출하고, 서한일 기준 유효기간 내에 있는 미국 유통 전 배치의 보관검체에 대해 전항목 화학·미생물 시험 실행계획·일정과 결과 요약을 제출한다(부적합 확인 시 고객 통지·제품 회수 등 신속한 시정조치).
공급업체 신뢰성·적격성평가, 자재 품질 이력 검토, 유효기간·재시험일의 타당성, 공급업체 적격성평가·부적격 처리 규정, 수명주기 모니터링을 포함한 자재 시스템 전반의 포괄적·독립적 검토를 수행하고, 이를 근거로 한 체계적 CAPA를 요약 제출한다.
입고 원료 로트별 확인·함량·품질·순도 시험 방법을 기술하고, 로트별 최소 1개 특정 확인 시험 실시를 약속하며, COA를 수용하려는 경우 초기 밸리데이션과 주기적 재밸리데이션으로 신뢰성을 확립하는 방안과 COA 밸리데이션 SOP·결과 요약을 제출한다.
21 CFR 211.34 에 따른 자격 있는 컨설턴트를 고용해 6개 시스템 전체 CGMP 감사를 받고, 원료·완제품 시험을 수행하는 계약 시설의 적격성평가·감독 프로그램을 요약 제출한다.

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: FDA는 2026년 8월 14일 귀사가 미국으로 수입 신청하는 모든 의약품을 수입경보(Import Alert) 66-40에 등재했다. 위반이 완전히 해결되고 CGMP 준수가 확인될 때까지 귀사를 제조소로 기재한 신규 허가신청 및 변경신청의 승인이 보류될 수 있으며, 시정조치 완료 확인을 위한 실사가 이뤄질 수 있다. 위반을 해결하지 못하면 FD&C Act 801(a)(3)에 따라 귀사 싱가포르 제조소 제품의 미국 반입 거부가 계속될 수 있고, 불량의약품으로 보이는 제품은 억류되거나 반입이 거부될 수 있다.

violations_ko.statement_ko: 귀사는 각 의약품 배치에 대해 출하 전에 각 유효성분의 확인(identity) 및 함량(strength)을 포함하여 의약품 최종 규격에 대한 적합성을 적절한 시험실 시험으로 판정하지 않았으며, 또한 불쾌미생물이 없어야 하는 각 의약품 배치에 대해 필요한 적절한 시험실 시험을 실시하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.165(a) and 211.165(b)).
귀사는 의약품의 각 원료에 대해 확인(identity)을 검증하는 시험을 최소 1개 이상 실시하지 않았다. 또한 귀사는 원료 공급업체 시험 분석의 신뢰성을 적절한 주기로 밸리데이션하고 확립하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.84(d)(1) and 211.84(d)(2)).
귀사의 품질부서는 제조된 의약품이 CGMP를 준수하고 확인(identity)·함량(strength)·품질(quality)·순도(purity)에 대해 설정된 규격을 충족하도록 보증할 책임을 이행하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.22).

3a5a9d3e0689.source_text: FDA Review Violations were identified and documented during review of your drug manufacturing facility, TSP Solutions Pte. Ltd., FDA Establishment Identifier (FEI) 3023093622. This review was conducted under FDA’s statutory authority and public health responsibilities to protect the public from unsafe, ineffective, and poor quality drugs. Your facility is registered with the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) as a manufacturer of over-the-counter (OTC) drug products. FDA has reviewed the records you submitted in response to our September 9, 2025, request and subsequent correspondence, for records and other information pursuant to section 704(a)(4) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) for your facility. This warning letter summarizes significant violations of Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) regulations for finished pharmaceuticals. See Title 21 Code of Federal Regulations, parts 210 and 211 (21 CFR, parts 210 and 211). Because your methods, facilities, or controls for manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding of drugs as described in your response to our 704(a)(4) request do not conform to CGMP, your drug products are adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) (21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B)). Violations of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act The following are violations identified during our review. As a reminder, this is not an all-inclusive list of violations at your facility. 1. Your firm failed to have, for each batch of drug product, appropriate laboratory determination of satisfactory conformance to final specifications for the drug product, including the identity and strength of each active ingredient, prior to release; and, your firm failed to conduct appropriate laboratory testing, as necessary, for each batch of drug product required to be free of objectionable microorganisms (21 CFR 211.165(a) and 211.165(b)). Your firm manufactures sunscreen drug products. Based on the records and information you provided, you did not demonstrate that you conduct adequate finished drug product testing on your drug products. Specifically, neither the certificate of analysis (COA) reports nor the batch records that you provided include an appropriate assay test for active ingredient content or impurity testing. In addition, your records do not include appropriate microbiological testing. Full release testing, including strength and identity testing of the active ingredient, as well as appropriate microbiological testing, must be performed before drug product release and distribution. Without adequate testing, you do not have adequate scientific evidence to ensure that your drug products conform to appropriate specifications before release. In response to this letter, provide: A list of chemical and microbial specifications, including test methods, used to analyze each batch of your drug products before a lot disposition decision. An action plan and timelines for conducting full chemical and microbiological testing of retain samples to determine the quality of all batches of drug product distributed to the United States that are within expiry as of the date of this letter. A summary of all results obtained from testing retain samples from each batch. If such testing reveals substandard quality drug products, take rapid corrective actions, such as notifying customers and product recalls. 2. Your firm failed to conduct at least one test to verify the identity of each component of a drug product. Your firm also failed to validate and establish the reliability of your component supplier’s test analyses at appropriate intervals (21 CFR 211.84(d)(1) and 211.84(d)(2)). Based on the records and information you provided, you did not demonstrate that you are adequately testing the identity of incoming components used in the manufacture of your drug products. Your response also indicated that you accept your supplier’s COA without verifying the test results at appropriate intervals. Verification of component quality is performed only by reviewing the COAs and material safety data sheets provided by the suppliers. Without adequate testing and without establishing the reliability of your component suppliers’ test analyses at appropriate intervals, you do not have scientific evidence that your raw materials conform to appropriate specifications before you use them in the manufacture of your drug products. As a manufacturer, you have a responsibility to sample, test, and examine drug components before you use them in production to ensure adequate quality. In response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive, independent review of your material system, including but not limited to: o evaluating all suppliers of materials (components, containers, and closures) to determine if they are reliable and appropriately qualified o an assessment of all materials to determine whether they are consistently of acceptable quality based on thorough historical review o a review to ensure assigned expiration or retest dates are appropriate (supported by data) o adequacy of the supplier qualification program, and its selection, qualification, and disqualification provisions o vigilant lifecycle monitoring of all suppliers using sound quality risk management practices o based on this thorough review, summarize a systemic CAPA that remediates the materials system to ensure ongoing lifecycle oversight of vendor performance and prevents use of unsuitable components (ingredients), containers and closures. The chemical and microbiological quality control specifications you use to test and release each incoming lot of component for use in manufacturing. A description of how you will test each component lot for conformity with all appropriate specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity. If you intend to accept any results from your supplier’s COA instead of testing each component lot for strength, quality, and purity, specify how you will robustly establish the reliability of your supplier’s results through initial validation as well as periodic re-validation. In addition, include a commitment to always conduct at least one specific identity test for each incoming component lot. A summary of results obtained from testing all components to evaluate the reliability of the COA from each component manufacturer. Include your SOP that describes this COA validation program. A summary of your program for qualifying and overseeing contract facilities that test the components and drug products you manufacture. 3. Your firm’s quality unit failed to exercise its responsibility to ensure drug products manufactured are in compliance with CGMP and meet established specifications for identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.22). Based on the records and information you provided, your firm failed to establish an adequate quality unit (QU) with the responsibilities and authority to oversee the manufacturing of drug products. For example, your QU failed to ensure: Adequate procedures ensuring appropriate production and process controls for drug product manufacturing and qualification of equipment used to manufacture drug products (21 CFR 211.100(a)). Adequate laboratory control procedures to ensure drug products conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality, and purity (21 CFR 211.160(b)). The establishment of an adequate, ongoing stability program (21 CFR 211.166(a)). Your firm’s quality systems are inadequate. For help implementing quality systems and risk management approaches to meet the requirements of CGMP regulations 21 CFR, parts 210 and 211, see FDA’s guidance documents Quality Systems Approach to Pharmaceutical CGMP Regulations at https://www.fda.gov/media/71023/download. CGMP Consultant Recommended Based upon the nature of the violations we identified in your response, you should engage a consultant qualified as set forth in 21 CFR 211.34 to evaluate your operations and to assist your firm in meeting CGMP requirements. The qualified consultant should also perform a comprehensive six-system audit of your entire operation for CGMP compliance and evaluate the completion and efficacy of your corrective actions and preventive actions before you pursue resolution of your firm’s compliance status with FDA. Your use of a consultant does not relieve your firm’s obligation to comply with CGMP. Your firm’s executive management remains responsible for resolving all deficiencies and systemic flaws to ensure ongoing CGMP compliance. Conclusion As previously stated, you are responsible for investigating and determining the root causes of any violations and implementing corrective and preventative measures to ensure future and sustained compliance so that these violations and any others do not occur. FDA placed all drugs and drug products offered for import into the United States from your firm on Import Alert 66-40 on August 14, 2026. FDA may withhold approval of new applications or supplements listing your firm as a drug manufacturer until any violations are completely addressed and we confirm your compliance with CGMP. We may inspect to verify that you have completed corrective actions to any violations. Failure to address any violations may also result in the FDA continuing to refuse admission of articles manufactured at TSP Solutions Pte. Ltd., at Block 998 Toa Payoh North, #05-05/06 Mapletree Industrial, Singapore 318993, Singapore, into the United States under section 801(a)(3) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 381(a)(3). Articles under this authority that appear to be adulterated may be detained or refused admission, in that the methods and controls used in their manufacture do not appear to conform to CGMP within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B). Send your written response to CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov within 15 business days of receipt of this letter. Identify your written response with FEI 3023093622 and ATTN: Bryce Hammer in the subject line of the email. If you have information that you believe demonstrates that your products are not in violation of the FD&C Act and FDA regulations, include that information for our consideration. FDA posts warning letters to www.FDA.gov. key_violations.original: Your firm failed to conduct adequate investigations and take appropriate corrective action when a failure of a production batch or any component of the batch failed to meet any of its specifications (21 CFR 212.20(d)). Inadequate Investigation of Out-of-Limit Environmental Monitoring Results Your firm failed to adequately investigate out-of-limit (OOL) environmental monitoring (EM) results, identify the root cause of recurring microbial recoveries, and implement appropriate corrective actions. EM data from March 2024 through April 2026 revealed an adverse trend with over 100 microbial recoveries from ISO 5 areas (e.g., (b)(4) and laminar airflow workstation (LAFW)), including counts of (b)(4) colony forming units (CFUs). These recoveries were not formally identified, preventing your firm from conducting adequate investigations. More than 90 ISO 5 isolates were documented as “resembles previously identified Bacillus colonies” or “resembles previously identified colonies” in lieu of formal microbial identification, with no record of which previously identified organism the colony purportedly resembled. Since December 2024, of approximately 75 ISO 5 microbial recoveries, only two were sent for formal identification. No genus or species recovered in ISO 5 areas has been recorded in your EM log since September 2025. Operator training for interpreting (b)(4) plate results consisted of a single presentation slide instructing personnel to “count CFUs and record results,” with no instruction regarding microbial identification. Additionally, (b)(4) ISO 7 cleanroom certification results for areas surrounding your (b)(4) and LAFW revealed microbial recoveries that exceeded your action limits and were not adequately investigated. For example, a (b)(4) CFU active air recovery described as bacterial and yeast was not adequately identified because the sample plates were received with (b)(4) on the lid. For a (b)(4) CFU recovery sent for identification, (b)(4) CFU were identified as Pseudopithomyces palmicola and the remaining (b)(4) CFU were identified as Micrococcus spp. and coryneform bacillus. Investigations were not initiated. Further, your (b)(4) product review acknowledges “excess CFUs as an ongoing issue in the (b)(4) cleanroom.”
key_violations.description: 귀사는 생산 배치 또는 그 배치의 구성요소가 규격 중 어느 하나라도 충족하지 못한 경우 적절한 조사를 실시하고 적절한 시정조치를 취하지 않았다(21 CFR 212.20(d)). 한도 초과 환경모니터링 결과에 대한 부적절한 조사 — 귀사는 한도 초과(OOL) 환경모니터링(EM) 결과를 적절히 조사하고, 반복적인 미생물 검출의 근본 원인을 규명하며, 적절한 시정조치를 시행하지 않았다. 2024년 3월부터 2026년 4월까지의 EM 데이터는 ISO 5 구역(예: (b)(4) 및 층류작업대(LAFW))에서 100건이 넘는 미생물 검출이라는 이상 경향을 보였으며, 여기에는 (b)(4) 집락형성단위(CFU)의 계수도 포함되었다. 이 검출균들은 공식적으로 동정되지 않았고, 이로 인해 귀사는 적절한 조사를 수행할 수 없었다. 90건이 넘는 ISO 5 분리균이 공식적인 미생물 동정 대신 “이전에 동정된 Bacillus 집락과 유사함” 또는 “이전에 동정된 집락과 유사함”으로 기록되었고, 해당 집락이 어떤 기동정 미생물과 유사하다는 것인지에 대한 기록은 없었다. 2024년 12월 이후 약 75건의 ISO 5 미생물 검출 중 공식 동정에 의뢰된 것은 단 2건이었다. 2025년 9월 이후로는 ISO 5 구역에서 검출된 어떤 속(genus)이나 종(species)도 귀사의 EM 로그에 기록되지 않았다. (b)(4) 플레이트 결과 판독에 대한 작업자 교육은 “CFU를 계수하고 결과를 기록하라”고 지시하는 프레젠테이션 슬라이드 한 장이 전부였으며, 미생물 동정에 관한 지침은 전혀 없었다. 또한 귀사의 (b)(4) 및 LAFW 주변 구역에 대한 (b)(4) ISO 7 클린룸 인증 결과에서 조치기준을 초과한 미생물 검출이 확인되었으나 적절히 조사되지 않았다. 예를 들어, 세균 및 효모로 기술된 (b)(4) CFU의 능동 공기 검출균은 검체 플레이트가 뚜껑에 (b)(4)가 있는 상태로 접수되어 적절히 동정되지 않았다. 동정에 의뢰된 (b)(4) CFU 검출균의 경우 (b)(4) CFU는 Pseudopithomyces palmicola로, 나머지 (b)(4) CFU는 Micrococcus spp. 및 코리네형 간균(coryneform bacillus)으로 동정되었다. 그럼에도 조사는 개시되지 않았다. 나아가 귀사의 (b)(4) 제품 검토 문서는 “(b)(4) 클린룸의 과다 CFU가 지속적인 문제”임을 인정하고 있다.
key_violations.risk: ISO 5 구역 미생물 검출균을 동정·조사하지 않아 포자형성균·진균 오염 경로를 파악할 수 없고, 무균시험 결과 확인 전에 투여되는 PET 의약품의 무균성 보증이 무너져 환자 감염 위험이 생긴다.

key_violations.original: You failed to conduct adequate effectiveness checks for CAPAs to prevent recurrence. Multiple CAPAs for recurring low (b)(4) yields were closed without your required effectiveness checks. Yields continued to fall below your established (b)(4) % limit. No investigations were initiated for approximately (b)(4) batches manufactured between August 2024 and April 2025 that failed the (b)(4) % limit, with yields as low as (b)(4) %. Rather than identifying and correcting the root cause, you lowered the yield limit from (b)(4) % to (b)(4) %. Yields subsequently fell below your revised (b)(4) % limit. Notably, Incident Report NNM 2025 08 states, “This has been an ongoing issue now for more than a year. We are continuing to evaluate the situation in an attempt to increase yields.” The effectiveness check for that incident was marked “No” with no additional corrective action identified. You continue to manufacture your PET drug without resolving the root cause of the low yields.
key_violations.description: 귀사는 재발 방지를 위한 CAPA의 효과성 점검을 적절히 수행하지 않았다. 반복되는 낮은 (b)(4) 수율에 대한 여러 CAPA가 귀사 스스로 요구하는 효과성 점검 없이 종결되었다. 수율은 계속해서 귀사가 설정한 (b)(4) % 한도를 밑돌았다. 2024년 8월부터 2025년 4월 사이에 제조되어 (b)(4) % 한도에 부적합한 약 (b)(4)개 배치에 대해 어떤 조사도 개시되지 않았으며, 수율은 (b)(4) %까지 낮았다. 귀사는 근본 원인을 규명하고 시정하는 대신 수율 한도를 (b)(4) %에서 (b)(4) %로 낮추었다. 이후 수율은 개정된 (b)(4) % 한도마저 밑돌았다. 특히 사건보고서(Incident Report) NNM 2025 08에는 “이 문제는 이제 1년 넘게 지속되고 있다. 수율을 높이기 위해 상황을 계속 평가하고 있다.”라고 기재되어 있다. 해당 사건에 대한 효과성 점검은 아무런 추가 시정조치 없이 “No”로 표시되었다. 귀사는 낮은 수율의 근본 원인을 해결하지 않은 채 PET 의약품 제조를 계속하고 있다.
key_violations.risk: 수율 저하는 공정이 관리 상태를 잃고 있다는 신호인데, 조사 없이 한도를 낮춰 부적합을 덮었으므로 공정 이상이 품질 결함으로 이어져도 탐지되지 않을 위험이 있다.

key_violations.original: Procedures to ensure that all equipment is clean, suitable for its intended purposes, properly installed, maintained, and capable of repeatedly producing valid results, are not adequately followed. (21 CFR 212.30(b)). Inadequate Control of Environmental Monitoring Plates You failed to adequately control your EM contact plates used to monitor your production operations. EM plates were stored inside a (b)(4) containing a significant amount of (b)(4) solution before and after sampling. You failed to assess the impact of this practice on microbial recovery. (b)(4) is a (b)(4) with well-documented sporicidal activity. Exposure of EM plates to (b)(4) can kill or suppress the microorganisms these tests are designed to recover, rendering results unreliable and potentially generating false negatives.
key_violations.description: 모든 설비가 청결하고, 의도한 목적에 적합하며, 적절히 설치·유지되고, 유효한 결과를 반복적으로 산출할 수 있도록 보장하는 절차가 적절히 준수되지 않았다(21 CFR 212.30(b)). 환경모니터링 플레이트의 부적절한 관리 — 귀사는 생산 작업을 모니터링하는 데 사용하는 EM 접촉 플레이트를 적절히 관리하지 않았다. EM 플레이트는 검체 채취 전후로 상당량의 (b)(4) 용액이 들어 있는 (b)(4) 안에 보관되었다. 귀사는 이러한 관행이 미생물 회수에 미치는 영향을 평가하지 않았다. (b)(4)는 살포자(sporicidal) 활성이 잘 알려진 (b)(4)이다. EM 플레이트가 (b)(4)에 노출되면 이 시험이 회수하도록 설계된 미생물이 사멸하거나 억제될 수 있어, 결과를 신뢰할 수 없게 만들고 위음성을 초래할 가능성이 있다.
key_violations.risk: 살포자제에 노출된 EM 플레이트로 얻은 과거 환경모니터링 데이터 전체의 신뢰성이 훼손되어, 그 데이터에 근거한 배치 출하 판정의 타당성도 담보할 수 없다.

key_violations.original: Your firm failed to ensure adequate control of airflow in the ISO 5 critical aseptic processing area. Smoke studies conducted at your facility did not include a dynamic evaluation of LAFW or (b)(4) operations and therefore do not adequately demonstrate that unidirectional airflow effectively controls air quality during aseptic manufacturing.
key_violations.description: 귀사는 ISO 5 핵심 무균공정 구역의 기류를 적절히 관리하지 않았다. 귀사 시설에서 실시한 기류 시각화 연구(스모크 스터디)는 LAFW 또는 (b)(4) 작업에 대한 동적(dynamic) 평가를 포함하지 않았으며, 따라서 무균 제조 중에 일방향 기류가 공기 품질을 효과적으로 관리한다는 것을 적절히 입증하지 못한다.
key_violations.risk: 실제 작업 조건에서 일방향 기류가 검증되지 않아 작업자 개입·물품 반입 시 ISO 5 구역으로 오염이 유입될 수 있으며, 무균 공정 전반의 무균성 보증 근거가 부족하다.

deep_analysis.fda_evaluation: FDA는 귀사의 2026년 6월 11일자 Form FDA 483 회신을 상세히 검토했으나, 지원 문서나 CGMP 준수를 위한 시정조치의 적절한 증거를 제시하지 않아 부적절하다고 평가했다. 항목별로 보면, ISO 5 검출균을 향후 동정·기록하겠다는 약속은 미동정 검출균의 소급 평가·이상 경향 평가, 동정 없이 이뤄진 과거 배치 출하 판정의 적절성 평가, ISO 등급 구역 내 포자형성균·진균 존재에 대한 대응이 없어 부적절하다. 효과성 점검 요건에 관한 재교육과 사건보고서 양식 완비 약속은 제조 배치의 소급 평가가 없고 지속적인 저수율의 근본 원인을 다루지 않으며 수율 한도 하향의 적절성도 다루지 않아 부적절하고, 교육만으로는 품질부서 감독이 결함 있는 조사를 탐지하지 못한 시스템적 실패를 해결할 수 없다고 지적했다. EM 플레이트 분무 중단·절차 개정은 과거 EM 데이터의 신뢰성과 이에 근거한 출하 판정을 평가하지 않았고, 스모크 스터디 개선 약속은 실제 LAFW 및 (b)(4) 작업의 동적 평가 부재를 다루지 않았으며, 소독 재교육은 문서화된 소독 절차를 무균 공정의 필수 단계로 확립하지 않아 모두 부적절하다고 판단했다. 아울러 2023년 12월 13일 규제 회의에서 유사한 CGMP 위반을 논의했음에도 반복된 점을 들어 경영진의 감독·통제가 부적절하다고 평가했다.

required_remediation.deadline: 서한 수령 후 15영업일 이내 CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov 로 서면 회신(서한 또는 이메일 제목에 FEI 3005334016 및 ATTN: Compliance officer Michael Klapal 기재).
items: 한도 설정, 검체 채취 방법·위치·빈도, 경향 분석, 일탈·이상 경향 조사를 포함한 EM 프로그램의 독립적·포괄적 검토와 그 결과에 근거한 종합 CAPA 계획을 제출한다.
일탈·불일치·불만·OOS·OOL·실패 조사 시스템 전반을 독립적으로 평가하고, 인력 역량·문서화된 절차·과학적 근거·근본 원인 평가·CAPA 효과성·품질부서 감독을 포괄하는 상세 개선 계획과 함께, 품질부서에 효과적 기능을 위한 권한과 자원을 부여하는 평가·개선 계획을 제출한다.
자격 있는 컨설턴트가 감독하는 미생물 검체 배지 취급 CAPA를 수립해, 고유 라벨링·취급자 서명·무결성 및 관리 연속성 추적·활동 일시 기록·플레이트 디지털 타임스탬프 사진·계수자 서명·품질보증 감독을 포함한 검체 관리 및 전체 대사(reconciliation) 체계를 갖춘다.
무균 공정·설비·시설의 오염 위해요소 전반에 대한 독립적 위험평가와 일정이 포함된 개선 계획을 제출하고, 시정 후 동적 조건에서 일방향 기류에 대한 스모크 스터디를 다시 수행하며 개선된 운영의 적격성평가·밸리데이션 계획을 기술한다.

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: 위반이 해결되지 않으면 다른 연방기관의 계약 수주가 제한될 수 있고, FDA가 수출증명서 발급을 보류할 수 있다. 위반이 완전히 해결되고 CGMP 준수가 확인될 때까지 귀사를 제조소로 기재한 신규 허가신청 및 변경신청의 승인이 보류될 수 있으며, 시정조치 완료를 확인하기 위한 재실사가 이뤄질 수 있다. 2023년 12월 13일 규제 회의 이후 반복된 위반이라는 점에서 추가 조치 위험이 커졌다. 공급 중단으로 이어질 수 있는 조치를 고려하는 경우 즉시 CDER 의약품 부족(Drug Shortages) 담당 부서에 연락하도록 요청받았다.

violations_ko.statement_ko: 귀사는 생산 배치 또는 그 배치의 구성요소가 규격 중 어느 하나라도 충족하지 못한 경우 적절한 조사를 실시하고 적절한 시정조치를 취하지 않았다(21 CFR 212.20(d)).
모든 설비가 청결하고 의도한 용도에 적합하며, 적절히 설치·유지관리되고 유효한 결과를 반복적으로 산출할 수 있도록 보장하는 절차가 제대로 준수되지 않는다(21 CFR 212.30(b)).

8909d4bb39b5.source_text: FDA Inspection Violations were observed and documented during an inspection of your drug manufacturing facility, Northland Nuclear Medicine, LLC, FDA Establishment Identifier (FEI) 3005334016, located at 1815 Michigan Ave., Bismarck, from May 26 to 29, 2026. This inspection was conducted under FDA’s statutory authority and public health responsibilities to protect the public from unsafe, ineffective, and poor quality drugs. This warning letter summarizes significant violations of Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) regulations for positron emission tomography (PET) drugs. See Title 21 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), part 212 (21 CFR part 212). Because your methods, facilities, or controls for manufacturing, processing, packaging, or holding do not conform to CGMP, your PET drug products are adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act), 21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B). We reviewed your June 11, 2026, response to our Form FDA 483 in detail. Your response is inadequate because you failed to provide supporting documentation for evaluation or adequate evidence of corrective actions taken to bring your operations into compliance with CGMP. Violations of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act The following are violations observed during our inspection and review. As a reminder, this is not an all-inclusive list of violations at your facility. 1. Your firm failed to conduct adequate investigations and take appropriate corrective action when a failure of a production batch or any component of the batch failed to meet any of its specifications (21 CFR 212.20(d)). Inadequate Investigation of Out-of-Limit Environmental Monitoring Results Your firm failed to adequately investigate out-of-limit (OOL) environmental monitoring (EM) results, identify the root cause of recurring microbial recoveries, and implement appropriate corrective actions. EM data from March 2024 through April 2026 revealed an adverse trend with over 100 microbial recoveries from ISO 5 areas (e.g., (b)(4) and laminar airflow workstation (LAFW)), including counts of (b)(4) colony forming units (CFUs). These recoveries were not formally identified, preventing your firm from conducting adequate investigations. More than 90 ISO 5 isolates were documented as “resembles previously identified Bacillus colonies” or “resembles previously identified colonies” in lieu of formal microbial identification, with no record of which previously identified organism the colony purportedly resembled. Since December 2024, of approximately 75 ISO 5 microbial recoveries, only two were sent for formal identification. No genus or species recovered in ISO 5 areas has been recorded in your EM log since September 2025. Operator training for interpreting (b)(4) plate results consisted of a single presentation slide instructing personnel to “count CFUs and record results,” with no instruction regarding microbial identification. Additionally, (b)(4) ISO 7 cleanroom certification results for areas surrounding your (b)(4) and LAFW revealed microbial recoveries that exceeded your action limits and were not adequately investigated. For example, a (b)(4) CFU active air recovery described as bacterial and yeast was not adequately identified because the sample plates were received with (b)(4) on the lid. For a (b)(4) CFU recovery sent for identification, (b)(4) CFU were identified as Pseudopithomyces palmicola and the remaining (b)(4) CFU were identified as Micrococcus spp. and coryneform bacillus. Investigations were not initiated. Further, your (b)(4) product review acknowledges “excess CFUs as an ongoing issue in the (b)(4) cleanroom.” Your firm systematically failed to adequately investigate out-of-limit environmental monitoring results, to identify root causes of recurring microbial contamination in critical ISO 5 areas, and to implement effective corrective action and preventive action (CAPA). In your response, you commit to ensuring that future microbial colony recoveries from ISO 5 areas will be properly identified and documented. Your response is inadequate because it does not include a retrospective assessment of the unidentified recoveries or an evaluation of adverse trends, does not assess the adequacy of past batch release decisions made in the absence of organism identification, and does not address the documented presence of spore-forming bacteria and fungi in your ISO-classified environments. Environmental isolate identification data provides essential information for an investigation into routes of contamination, such as when investigating an adverse environmental control trend, media fill contamination, or a product sterility testing failure. EM should include routine identification of microorganisms to the species (or, where appropriate, genus) level, including isolates recovered from an ISO 5 environment, its surrounding cleanroom, and personnel. It is essential that cleaning and disinfection procedures are described in sufficient detail, including the preparation, disinfectant selection, and contact time to enable reproducibility and ensure that potential contaminants are adequately removed from surfaces. The effectiveness of disinfection procedures should be evaluated through a routine EM program, and adverse trends should prompt reassessment of disinfectant selection, concentration, contact time, and application frequency. Inadequate Investigation and CAPA for Recurring Manufacturing Deficiencies You failed to conduct adequate effectiveness checks for CAPAs to prevent recurrence. Multiple CAPAs for recurring low (b)(4) yields were closed without your required effectiveness checks. Yields continued to fall below your established (b)(4) % limit. No investigations were initiated for approximately (b)(4) batches manufactured between August 2024 and April 2025 that failed the (b)(4) % limit, with yields as low as (b)(4) %. Rather than identifying and correcting the root cause, you lowered the yield limit from (b)(4) % to (b)(4) %. Yields subsequently fell below your revised (b)(4) % limit. Notably, Incident Report NNM 2025 08 states, “This has been an ongoing issue now for more than a year. We are continuing to evaluate the situation in an attempt to increase yields.” The effectiveness check for that incident was marked “No” with no additional corrective action identified. You continue to manufacture your PET drug without resolving the root cause of the low yields. PET drug producers must establish appropriate action limits for radiochemical yield and investigate and correct the root cause when those limits are exceeded. Low yields or a downward trend in yield are recognized indicators that the production process may be losing control. Lowering a yield limit to accommodate a failing process does not satisfy this requirement. Producers must maintain adequate production and process controls to ensure consistent production and must implement appropriate CAPA to prevent recurrence of nonconforming results. In your response, you commit to retrain manufacturing personnel on effectiveness check requirements and to formally complete the incident report form. Your response is inadequate because you have not conducted a retrospective evaluation of the batches manufactured and it fails to address the root cause of the persistent low-yield problem. Additionally, your response does not address the adequacy of lowering your yield limit from (b)(4) % to (b)(4) % as a corrective measure in lieu of identifying and resolving the root cause of persistent yield failures. To ensure proper root cause analysis and appropriate CAPA implementation, investigations must be thorough, well-documented, scientifically sound, and timely. Training alone does not address the systemic failures that allowed deficient investigations to persist undetected by quality unit (QU) oversight. In response to this letter, provide: An independent, comprehensive review of your EM program to ensure vigilant, timely detection and response to potential product contamination hazards in your manufacturing environment. This assessment should include, but not be limited to: o establishing appropriate limits, o sampling methods, o sampling locations and frequencies, o trend analysis, o appropriate investigation of deviations and adverse trends, o and a comprehensive CAPA plan based on the findings of the assessment. A comprehensive, independent assessment of your overall system for investigating deviations, discrepancies, complaints, OOS results, OOL results, and failures. Provide a detailed action plan to remediate this system, encompassing the following: o staff competencies (including use of appropriate subject matter experts) o written procedures o scientific rigor and foundation o scope determination o root cause evaluations o CAPA effectiveness o quality unit lead functional roles, and oversight to ensure all phases of investigations are appropriately conducted. o and, based on above, detailed systemic improvements to the investigation system A comprehensive assessment and remediation plan to ensure your QU is given the authority and resources to effectively function. The assessment should also include, but not be limited to: o a determination of whether procedures used by your firm are robust and o appropriate o provisions for QU oversight throughout your operations to evaluate o adherence to appropriate practices o a complete and final review of each batch and its related information before the QU disposition decision o oversight and approval of investigations and discharging of all other QU duties to ensure identity, strength, quality, and purity of all products 2. Procedures to ensure that all equipment is clean, suitable for its intended purposes, properly installed, maintained, and capable of repeatedly producing valid results, are not adequately followed. (21 CFR 212.30(b)). Inadequate Control of Environmental Monitoring Plates You failed to adequately control your EM contact plates used to monitor your production operations. EM plates were stored inside a (b)(4) containing a significant amount of (b)(4) solution before and after sampling. You failed to assess the impact of this practice on microbial recovery. (b)(4) is a (b)(4) with well-documented sporicidal activity. Exposure of EM plates to (b)(4) can kill or suppress the microorganisms these tests are designed to recover, rendering results unreliable and potentially generating false negatives. In your response, you state that personnel have stopped spraying EM plates and that procedures have been updated accordingly. Your response is inadequate because it does not address the reliability of historical EM data collected using the compromised methodology, does not include a retrospective assessment of past EM results that were affected by (b)(4) exposure, and does not evaluate the adequacy of prior batch release decisions made in the absence of reliable environmental monitoring data. Inadequate Airflow Visualization Studies (Smoke Studies) Your firm failed to ensure adequate control of airflow in the ISO 5 critical aseptic processing area. Smoke studies conducted at your facility did not include a dynamic evaluation of LAFW or (b)(4) operations and therefore do not adequately demonstrate that unidirectional airflow effectively controls air quality during aseptic manufacturing. Adequate contamination control in an aseptic PET drug manufacturing environment requires that monitoring tools, disinfection practices, and airflow qualification studies be designed and executed in a manner that meaningfully protects the sterility of the product. Compromised environmental monitoring media, inadequate airflow qualification, and failure to disinfect product-contact surfaces prior to aseptic operations collectively undermine the sterility assurance of your PET drugs. In your response, you commit to include transfer of starting components and materials prior to mock operations going forward. Your response is inadequate because you do not address the absence of a validated, dynamic evaluation of actual LAFW and (b)(4) operations under representative conditions. Failure to Adequately Disinfect (b)(4) You failed to adequately disinfect the exterior surfaces of the (b)(4) prior to aseptic manufacturing operations and failed to establish written procedures for the cleaning and disinfection of (b)(4) surfaces. In your response, you indicate that personnel were informed and retrained on the procedures for proper disinfection. Your response is inadequate because it does not establish a written disinfection procedure for the (b)(4) as a required step in your aseptic manufacturing process. PET drug products have short expiry periods. Consequently, PET drug products are released and administered before the results of batch specific sterility testing and EM are known. Your ongoing EM program is essential to detect and respond to potential product contamination hazards in your manufacturing environment in a timely manner. Loss of environmental control in an aseptic manufacturing facility can ultimately pose a serious hazard to patients. Cleaning and disinfection should be performed frequently to ensure consistent control of environmental quality. In response to this letter, provide: A comprehensive CAPA, overseen by a qualified consultant, for handling microbiological sampling media to ensure robust and reliable data. Establish a system that ensures uninterrupted custody and full reconciliation of all microbiological samples, including but not limited to: o unique labeling of each sample o signatures of all staff who handle the sample o complete tracking of sample integrity and custody o date and time of each activity (e.g., sample collection, delivery, incubation, removal from incubator) o digital time-stamped photos of all plates o signatures of personnel performing reading of microbial counts o provisions for verifications and routine quality assurance oversight. Comprehensive, independent risk assessment of all contamination hazards with respect to your aseptic processes, equipment, and facilities, including but not limited to: o all human interactions within the ISO 5 area (e.g., risk reduction or elimination of manual interventions wherever possible) o equipment suitability (e.g., reliability, capability, ergonomics, placement) and sufficient cleanroom space o air quality in the ISO 5 area and surrounding room including, but not limited to, air volume and flow o facility layout o personnel Flow and Material Flow (movement throughout all rooms used to conduct and support sterile operations, and all material transfers) o disinfection practices and procedures o specific CAPA recommendations that will comprehensively address the design and control hazards identified in the risk assessment A thorough, independent evaluation of airflow unidirectionality in your aseptic process. Ensure smoke studies are conducted under dynamic conditions, with comprehensive evaluations of aseptic processing airflow unidirectionality, including the impact of aseptic interventions and surrounding cleanroom hazards. Conduct the smoke studies after you remediate your aseptic operation, using proper practices (e.g., neutrally buoyant media) to appropriately visualize airflow. A detailed remediation plan with timelines to address the findings of the contamination hazards risk assessment. Describe specific tangible improvements to be made to aseptic processing operation design and control at your facility and explain how this CAPA plan will robustly remediate your deficient sterile manufacturing operations. Include comprehensive changes to the design of both your aseptic processing lines and cleanrooms. Also, describe your plans for qualification and validation of your extensively remediated operations. Repeat Violations at Facility In a regulatory meeting held on December 13, 2023, FDA discussed similar CGMP violations. You proposed specific remediation for these violations. Repeated failures demonstrate that executive management oversight and control over the manufacture of drugs is inadequate. Guidance on PET Drugs See FDA’s guidance document, PET Drugs—Current Good Manufacturing Practice , to help you meet the CGMP requirements when manufacturing PET drugs, at https://www.fda.gov/media/71013/download. This guidance document also references FDA’s guidance document, Sterile Drug Products Produced by Aseptic Processing—Current Good Manufacturing Practice for additional concepts and expectations that may apply to PET drug manufacturing, at https://www.fda.gov/media/71026/download. CGMP Consultant Recommended Based upon the nature of the violations we identified at your firm, you should engage a consultant qualified to evaluate your operations and to assist your firm in meeting CGMP requirements. The qualified consultant should also perform a comprehensive audit of your entire operation for CGMP compliance and evaluate the completion and efficacy of your corrective actions and preventive actions before you pursue resolution of your firm’s compliance status with FDA. Your use of a consultant does not relieve your firm’s obligation to comply with CGMP. Your firm’s executive management remains responsible for resolving all deficiencies and systemic flaws to ensure ongoing CGMP compliance. Conclusion You are responsible for investigating and determining the root causes of any violations and implementing corrective and preventative measures to ensure future and sustained compliance so that these violations and any others do not occur. Unresolved violations may prevent other Federal agencies from awarding contracts. Failure to address violations may also cause FDA to withhold issuance of Export Certificates. FDA may withhold approval of new applications or supplements listing your firm as a drug manufacturer until any violations are completely addressed and we confirm your compliance with CGMP. We may re-inspect to verify that you have completed corrective actions to address any violations. If you are considering an action that is likely to lead to a disruption in the supply of drugs produced at your facility, FDA requests that you contact CDER’s Drug Shortages Staff immediately, at drugshortages@fda.hhs.gov, so that FDA can work with you on the most effective way to bring your operations into compliance with the law. Contacting the Drug Shortages Staff also allows you to meet any obligations you may have to report discontinuances or interruptions in your drug manufacture under 21 U.S.C. 356c(b). This also allows FDA to consider, as soon as possible, what actions, if any, may be needed to avoid shortages and protect the health of patients who depend on your products. Send your written response to CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of this letter. Identify your written response with FEI 3005334016 and ATTN: Compliance officer Michael Klapal in the letter or in the subject line of the email. If you have information that you believe demonstrates that your products are not in violation of the FD&C Act and FDA regulations, include that information for our consideration. FDA posts warning letters to www.FDA.gov. Sincerely, /S/ Francis Godwin Director Office of Manufacturing Quality Office of Compliance Center for Drug Evaluation and Research U.S. Food and Drug Administration Content current as of: 10/27/2026 Regulated Product(s) Drugs Feedback FDA Archive About FDA Accessibility Visitor Information Website Policies / Privacy No FEAR Act Vulnerability Disclosure Policy FOIA HHS.gov USA.gov Contact FDA Follow FDA on Facebook Follow FDA on X Follow FDA on Instagram Follow FDA on LinkedIn View FDA videos on YouTube Subscribe to FDA RSS feeds Contact Number 1-888-INFO-FDA (1-888-463-6332) Back to Top

key_violations.original: Your firm failed to conduct at least one test to verify the identity of each component of a drug product (21 CFR 211.84(d)(1)). Your firm manufactures OTC drug products including (b)(4) . Based on the records and information you provided, you did not demonstrate that you adequately tested the identity of incoming components (e.g., (b)(4) ) used in the manufacture of your drug products. (b)(4) You failed to adequately test your incoming (b)(4) , used as an active ingredient in your drug products, for (b)(4) . The use of (b)(4) contaminated with (b)(4) has resulted in various lethal poisoning incidents in humans worldwide. See FDA’s guidance document (b)(4) . (b)(4) Identity testing for (b)(4) and certain other high-risk drug components includes a limit test in the United States Pharmacopeia (USP) to ensure that the components meet the relevant safety limits for levels of (b)(4) . Because you did not perform identity testing on each shipment of each lot using the USP identification test that detects these hazardous impurities, you failed to assure the acceptability of these components for use in the manufacture of your drug products. The use of ingredients contaminated with (b)(4) has resulted in various lethal poisoning incidents in humans worldwide. See FDA’s guidance document (b)(4) . Without adequate testing, you do not have scientific evidence that your components conform to appropriate specifications prior to use in the manufacture of your drug products.
key_violations.description: 귀사는 의약품의 각 원료에 대해 확인(identity)을 검증하는 시험을 최소 1개 이상 실시하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.84(d)(1)). 귀사는 (b)(4)을(를) 포함한 OTC 의약품을 제조한다. 귀사가 제출한 기록과 정보에 근거할 때, 귀사는 의약품 제조에 사용되는 입고 원료(예: (b)(4))의 확인 시험을 적절히 수행했음을 입증하지 못했다. (b)(4) — 귀사는 의약품의 유효성분으로 사용되는 입고 (b)(4)에 대해 (b)(4) 시험을 적절히 실시하지 않았다. (b)(4)에 오염된 (b)(4)의 사용은 전 세계적으로 사람에게 여러 건의 치명적 중독 사고를 일으켰다. FDA 가이던스 문서 (b)(4)를 참조하라. (b)(4) — (b)(4) 및 기타 특정 고위험 의약품 원료에 대한 확인 시험에는 원료가 (b)(4) 수준에 관한 해당 안전 한도를 충족하는지 보장하기 위한 미국약전(USP)의 한도시험이 포함된다. 귀사는 이러한 유해 불순물을 검출하는 USP 확인시험을 사용하여 각 로트의 각 입고분마다 확인 시험을 수행하지 않았으므로, 이 원료들이 의약품 제조에 사용하기에 적합함을 보증하지 못했다. (b)(4)에 오염된 성분의 사용은 전 세계적으로 사람에게 여러 건의 치명적 중독 사고를 일으켰다. FDA 가이던스 문서 (b)(4)를 참조하라. 적절한 시험 없이는 원료가 의약품 제조에 사용되기 전에 적절한 규격에 적합하다는 과학적 근거를 갖출 수 없다.
key_violations.risk: 고위험 원료에 대해 유해 불순물을 검출하는 USP 확인시험을 하지 않아, 치명적 중독 사고를 일으킨 바 있는 오염 원료가 유효성분으로 제품에 투입될 수 있다.

key_violations.original: Your firm failed to establish written procedures for production and process control designed to assure that the drug products you manufacture have the identity, strength, quality, and purity they purport or are represented to possess (21 CFR 211.100(a)). Based on the records and information you provided, you did not demonstrate that your manufacturing processes are reproducible and controlled to yield a product of uniform character and quality. Specifically, your response states that your firm does not have process validation procedures or process validation studies. Process validation evaluates the soundness of design and state of control of a process throughout its lifecycle. Each significant stage of a manufacturing process must be designed appropriately and assure the quality of raw material inputs, in-process materials, and finished drugs. Process qualification studies include intensive monitoring and testing of throughout each significant process stage to characterize intra-batch variation and evaluates batches to determine whether an initial state of control has been established. Successful process qualification studies are necessary before commercial distribution. Thereafter, ongoing vigilant oversight of process performance and product quality is necessary to ensure you maintain a stable manufacturing operation throughout the product lifecycle.
key_violations.description: 귀사는 제조하는 의약품이 표방하거나 보유한다고 표시된 확인(identity)·함량(strength)·품질(quality)·순도(purity)를 갖추도록 설계된 생산 및 공정 관리에 관한 문서화된 절차를 수립하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.100(a)). 귀사가 제출한 기록과 정보에 근거할 때, 귀사는 제조공정이 균일한 특성과 품질의 제품을 생산하도록 재현 가능하고 관리되고 있음을 입증하지 못했다. 구체적으로, 귀사의 회신에는 귀사에 공정 밸리데이션 절차나 공정 밸리데이션 연구가 없다고 기재되어 있다. 공정 밸리데이션은 수명주기 전반에 걸쳐 공정 설계의 타당성과 관리 상태를 평가한다. 제조공정의 각 주요 단계는 적절히 설계되어야 하며 원료 투입물, 공정 중 물질 및 완제의약품의 품질을 보증해야 한다. 공정 적격성평가 연구에는 배치 내 변동을 특성화하기 위한 각 주요 공정 단계 전반의 집중적인 모니터링과 시험이 포함되며, 초기 관리 상태가 확립되었는지 판단하기 위해 배치들을 평가한다. 상업적 유통 전에 공정 적격성평가 연구를 성공적으로 완료해야 한다. 그 이후에도 제품 수명주기 전반에 걸쳐 안정적인 제조 운영을 유지하려면 공정 성능과 제품 품질에 대한 지속적이고 면밀한 감독이 필요하다.
key_violations.risk: 공정 밸리데이션 절차·연구가 전무해 배치 간·배치 내 품질 균일성을 보증할 근거가 없으며, 이미 유통된 제품의 품질 일관성도 입증되지 않는다.

key_violations.original: Your firm failed to establish an adequate quality control unit with the responsibility and authority to approve or reject all components, drug product containers, closures, in-process materials, packaging materials, labeling, and drug products (21 CFR 211.22(a)). Based on the records and information you provided, your firm failed to establish an adequate quality unit (QU) with the responsibilities and authority to oversee the manufacturing of drug products. For example, your QU failed to ensure: Adequate laboratory control procedures to ensure drug products conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality and purity (21 CFR 211.160(b). Specifically, the records you provided demonstrate that you lack an adequate (b)(4) system monitoring program. The procedures you provided and (b)(4) test results lacked adequate testing for attributes such as (b)(4) . The establishment of an adequate ongoing stability program (21 CFR 211.166(a)). For example, the records and information you provided lacked complete stability data and complete stability testing. Specifically, your records did not document viscosity, pH, assay, and microbiological testing to ensure that your drug products meet all quality attributes throughout their shelf-life.
key_violations.description: 귀사는 모든 원료, 의약품 용기, 마개, 공정 중 물질, 포장재, 표시재료 및 의약품을 승인하거나 거부할 책임과 권한을 가진 적절한 품질관리부서를 수립하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.22(a)). 귀사가 제출한 기록과 정보에 근거할 때, 귀사는 의약품 제조를 감독할 책임과 권한을 갖춘 적절한 품질부서(QU)를 수립하지 않았다. 예를 들어, 귀사의 QU는 다음 사항을 보증하지 못했다. 의약품이 확인·함량·품질·순도에 관한 적절한 기준에 적합하도록 보장하는 적절한 시험실 관리 절차(21 CFR 211.160(b)). 구체적으로, 귀사가 제출한 기록은 적절한 (b)(4) 시스템 모니터링 프로그램이 없음을 보여준다. 귀사가 제출한 절차와 (b)(4) 시험 결과에는 (b)(4) 등의 항목에 대한 적절한 시험이 빠져 있었다. 적절하고 지속적인 안정성 시험 프로그램의 수립(21 CFR 211.166(a)). 예를 들어, 귀사가 제출한 기록과 정보에는 완전한 안정성 데이터와 완전한 안정성 시험이 없었다. 구체적으로, 귀사의 기록에는 의약품이 유효기간 전반에 걸쳐 모든 품질 특성을 충족함을 보증하기 위한 점도, pH, 정량(assay) 및 미생물 시험이 기록되어 있지 않았다.
key_violations.risk: (b)(4) 시스템 모니터링과 안정성 시험(점도·pH·정량·미생물)이 부재해 제조용 유틸리티 품질과 유효기간 동안의 제품 품질을 모두 보증할 수 없다.

deep_analysis.fda_evaluation: FDA는 2025년 9월 9일자 704(a)(4) 기록 요청과 후속 서신에 따라 귀사가 제출한 기록·정보를 검토한 결과, 귀사의 방법·시설·관리가 CGMP에 부합하지 않아 의약품이 불량(adulterated)에 해당한다고 판단했다. 제출 기록으로는 입고 원료의 확인 시험, 특히 유해 불순물을 검출하는 USP 확인시험을 각 로트의 각 입고분마다 수행했음을 입증하지 못했고, 귀사의 회신 스스로 공정 밸리데이션 절차나 연구가 없다고 밝혀 제조공정의 재현성과 관리 상태가 입증되지 않았다고 평가했다. 또한 품질부서가 시험실 관리 절차와 지속적인 안정성 프로그램을 보증하지 못해 품질 시스템 전체가 부적절하다고 판단했다. 위반의 성격상 미국 시장용 의약품 제조를 재개하려면 21 CFR 211.34에 따른 자격 있는 컨설턴트를 고용해 6개 시스템 전체 감사와 CAPA 완료·효과성 평가를 받을 것을 권고했으며, 컨설턴트 고용이 경영진의 CGMP 준수 책임을 면제하지 않는다고 명시했다.

required_remediation.deadline: 서한 수령 후 15영업일 이내 CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov 로 서면 회신(서한 또는 이메일 제목에 FEI 3016897521 및 ATTN: Daniel W. Brisker 기재).
items: 모든 위반의 근본 원인을 조사·규명하고, 해당 위반과 그 밖의 위반이 재발하지 않도록 지속적 준수를 보장하는 시정 및 예방 조치를 시행한다.
고위험 원료를 포함한 입고 원료에 대해 유해 불순물을 검출하는 USP 확인시험을 사용하여 각 로트의 각 입고분마다 확인 시험을 수행하는 체계를 갖춘다.
공정 밸리데이션 절차를 수립하고 상업적 유통 전에 공정 적격성평가 연구를 성공적으로 완료하며, 이후 공정 성능과 제품 품질을 지속적으로 감독하는 체계를 마련한다.
미국 시장용 제조 재개를 의도한다면 21 CFR 211.34 에 따른 자격 있는 컨설턴트를 고용해 6개 시스템 전체 CGMP 감사와 CAPA 완료·효과성 평가를 받은 뒤 FDA와 준수 상태 해결을 추진한다.

deep_analysis.administrative_risks: FDA는 2026년 9월 21일 귀사가 미국으로 수입 신청하는 모든 의약품을 수입경보(Import Alert) 66-40에 등재했다. 위반이 완전히 해결되고 CGMP 준수가 확인될 때까지 귀사를 제조소로 기재한 신규 허가신청 및 변경신청의 승인이 보류될 수 있으며, 시정조치 완료 확인을 위한 실사가 이뤄질 수 있다. 위반을 해결하지 못하면 FD&C Act 801(a)(3)에 따라 귀사 중국 저장성 제조소 제품의 미국 반입 거부가 계속될 수 있고, 불량의약품으로 보이는 제품은 억류되거나 반입이 거부될 수 있다.

violations_ko.statement_ko: 귀사는 의약품의 각 원료에 대해 확인(identity)을 검증하는 시험을 최소 1개 이상 실시하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.84(d)(1)).
귀사는 제조하는 의약품이 표방하거나 보유한다고 표시된 확인(identity)·함량(strength)·품질(quality)·순도(purity)를 갖추도록 설계된 생산 및 공정 관리에 관한 문서화된 절차를 수립하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.100(a)).
귀사는 모든 원료, 의약품 용기, 마개, 공정 중 물질, 포장재, 표시재료 및 의약품을 승인하거나 거부할 책임과 권한을 가진 적절한 품질관리부서를 수립하지 않았다(21 CFR 211.22(a)).

c9f381687575.source_text: FDA Review Violations were identified and documented during review of your drug manufacturing facility, Sanrace Biotechnology Co., Ltd., FDA Establishment Identifier (FEI) 3016897521. This review was conducted under FDA’s statutory authority and public health responsibilities to protect the public from unsafe, ineffective, and poor-quality drugs. Your facility is registered with the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) as a manufacturer of over-the-counter (OTC) drug products. FDA has reviewed the records you submitted in response to our September 9, 2025 request and subsequent correspondence, for records and other information pursuant to section 704(a)(4) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) for your facility. This warning letter summarizes significant violations of Current Good Manufacturing Practice (CGMP) regulations for finished pharmaceuticals. See Title 21 Code of Federal Regulations, parts 210 and 211 (21 CFR, parts 210 and 211). Because your methods, facilities, or controls for manufacturing, processing, packing, or holding of drugs, as described in your response to our 704(a)(4) request, do not conform to CGMP, your drug products are adulterated within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) (21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B)). Violations of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act The following are violations identified during our review. As a reminder, this is not an all-inclusive list of violations at your facility. 1. Your firm failed to conduct at least one test to verify the identity of each component of a drug product (21 CFR 211.84(d)(1)). Your firm manufactures OTC drug products including (b)(4) . Based on the records and information you provided, you did not demonstrate that you adequately tested the identity of incoming components (e.g., (b)(4) ) used in the manufacture of your drug products. (b)(4) You failed to adequately test your incoming (b)(4) , used as an active ingredient in your drug products, for (b)(4) . The use of (b)(4) contaminated with (b)(4) has resulted in various lethal poisoning incidents in humans worldwide. See FDA’s guidance document (b)(4) . (b)(4) Identity testing for (b)(4) and certain other high-risk drug components includes a limit test in the United States Pharmacopeia (USP) to ensure that the components meet the relevant safety limits for levels of (b)(4) . Because you did not perform identity testing on each shipment of each lot using the USP identification test that detects these hazardous impurities, you failed to assure the acceptability of these components for use in the manufacture of your drug products. The use of ingredients contaminated with (b)(4) has resulted in various lethal poisoning incidents in humans worldwide. See FDA’s guidance document (b)(4) . Without adequate testing, you do not have scientific evidence that your components conform to appropriate specifications prior to use in the manufacture of your drug products. 2. Your firm failed to establish written procedures for production and process control designed to assure that the drug products you manufacture have the identity, strength, quality, and purity they purport or are represented to possess (21 CFR 211.100(a)). Based on the records and information you provided, you did not demonstrate that your manufacturing processes are reproducible and controlled to yield a product of uniform character and quality. Specifically, your response states that your firm does not have process validation procedures or process validation studies. Process validation evaluates the soundness of design and state of control of a process throughout its lifecycle. Each significant stage of a manufacturing process must be designed appropriately and assure the quality of raw material inputs, in-process materials, and finished drugs. Process qualification studies include intensive monitoring and testing of throughout each significant process stage to characterize intra-batch variation and evaluates batches to determine whether an initial state of control has been established. Successful process qualification studies are necessary before commercial distribution. Thereafter, ongoing vigilant oversight of process performance and product quality is necessary to ensure you maintain a stable manufacturing operation throughout the product lifecycle. See FDA’s guidance document Process Validation: General Principles and Practices for general principles and approaches that FDA considers appropriate elements of process validation, at https://www.fda.gov/media/71021/download. 3. Your firm failed to establish an adequate quality control unit with the responsibility and authority to approve or reject all components, drug product containers, closures, in-process materials, packaging materials, labeling, and drug products (21 CFR 211.22(a)). Based on the records and information you provided, your firm failed to establish an adequate quality unit (QU) with the responsibilities and authority to oversee the manufacturing of drug products. For example, your QU failed to ensure: Adequate laboratory control procedures to ensure drug products conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality and purity (21 CFR 211.160(b). Specifically, the records you provided demonstrate that you lack an adequate (b)(4) system monitoring program. The procedures you provided and (b)(4) test results lacked adequate testing for attributes such as (b)(4) . The establishment of an adequate ongoing stability program (21 CFR 211.166(a)). For example, the records and information you provided lacked complete stability data and complete stability testing. Specifically, your records did not document viscosity, pH, assay, and microbiological testing to ensure that your drug products meet all quality attributes throughout their shelf-life. Your firm’s quality systems are inadequate. For help implementing quality systems and risk management approaches to meet the requirements of CGMP regulations 21 CFR, parts 210 and 211, see FDA’s guidance documents Quality Systems Approach to Pharmaceutical CGMP Regulations at https://www.fda.gov/media/71023/download. CGMP Consultant Recommended Based upon the nature of the violations we identified at your firm, you should engage a consultant qualified as set forth in 21 CFR 211.34 to evaluate your operations and to assist your firm in meeting CGMP requirements if your firm intends to resume manufacturing drugs for the U.S. market. The qualified consultant should also perform a comprehensive six-system audit of your entire operation for CGMP compliance and evaluate the completion and efficacy of your corrective actions and preventive actions before you pursue resolution of your firm’s compliance status with FDA. Your use of a consultant does not relieve your firm’s obligation to comply with CGMP. Your firm’s executive management remains responsible for resolving all deficiencies and systemic flaws to ensure ongoing CGMP compliance. Conclusion As previously stated, you are responsible for investigating and determining the root causes of any violations and implementing corrective and preventative measures to ensure future and sustained compliance so that these violations and any others do not occur. FDA placed all drugs and drug products offered for import into the United States from your firm on Import Alert 66-40 on September 21, 2026. FDA may withhold approval of new applications or supplements listing your firm as a drug manufacturer until any violations are completely addressed and we confirm your compliance with CGMP. We may inspect to verify that you have completed corrective actions to any violations. Failure to address any violations may also result in the FDA continuing to refuse admission of articles manufactured at Sanrace Biotechnology Co., Ltd., 268 Yanzhou Road, Lanxi Development Zone Lanxi, Jinhua, Zhejiang Province, 321102 China into the United States under section 801(a)(3) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 381(a)(3). Articles under this authority that appear to be adulterated may be detained or refused admission, in that the methods and controls used in their manufacture do not appear to conform to CGMP within the meaning of section 501(a)(2)(B) of the FD&C Act, 21 U.S.C. 351(a)(2)(B). Send your written response to CDER-OC-OMQ-Communications@fda.hhs.gov within 15 business days of receipt of this letter. Identify your written response with FEI 3016897521 and ATTN: Daniel W. Brisker in the letter or in the subject line of the email. If you have information that you believe demonstrates that your products are not in violation of the FD&C Act and FDA regulations, include that information for our consideration. FDA posts warning letters to www.FDA.gov. Sincerely, /S/ Francis Godwin Director Office of Manufacturing Quality Office of Compliance Center for Drug Evaluation and Research U.S. Food and Drug Administration cc: Registered US Agent: Mr. Manoj Zacharias Liberty Management Group Ltd.
